title: Private AI for Business: Implementation & Knowledge Search
description: Private AI implementation for company documents, SOPs and training. Plan permissions, deployment and costs with Yudaro in Houston and across Texas.
intro: Give employees a practical way to find approved company information while keeping deployment, access and review decisions under your control.

sections.title: What is private AI for a business?
sections.body: Private AI is an AI system deployed with controls over its models, data sources, users and infrastructure. It can retrieve approved company documents and help employees interpret them. A private deployment may run on customer hardware or controlled hosted infrastructure; the actual data flow, model provider, retention settings and access controls determine its privacy properties.

sections.title: Which problems should the first project solve?
sections.body: Start where employees repeatedly search for the same approved information. A distributor may need product specifications; a service business may need equipment procedures; a restaurant may need station training. Choose a small, maintained document collection before introducing live ERP access.
items: SOP retrieval: show the source procedure, revision and permitted next steps.
Product support: compare documented specifications and flag missing information.
Training: answer role-specific questions using approved onboarding material.
Management: summarize permitted reports with their date, filters and source totals.

sections.title: How does Yudaro implement a knowledge assistant?
sections.body: Discovery establishes the users, information owners and questions worth answering. We map permissions, clean source documents, choose infrastructure and configure retrieval. A pilot uses a business-owned evaluation set: common questions, outdated documents, conflicting answers and requests a user must not be allowed to see. Release follows documented acceptance and employee training.
items: Define source ownership and update responsibilities.
Test answers against original documents, including unsupported questions.
Enforce permissions at retrieval, not only at the user interface.
Agree monitoring, backup, recovery and change-management ownership.

sections.title: Local hardware or controlled hosting?
sections.body: Compare the full operating model, not only where a model runs. Local hardware requires maintenance and recovery planning. Hosted infrastructure requires review of providers and outbound data paths.

rows: Size for model, context and concurrent users
Review OCR, embeddings and telemetry too
Review tenancy, retention and external services

sections.title: What affects price, timing and success?
sections.body: Published AI Foundation starts at $7,500; AI Growth has a typical starting point of $15,000; AI Enterprise is scoped from $30,000. These are planning estimates. Source cleanup, document volume, permissions, hardware and integrations affect cost. A focused pilot can be planned in weeks; complex deployments require a phased schedule after discovery. Measure source accuracy, retrieval success, permission-test results, adoption and handling time.

sections.title: What should your team prepare?
sections.body: Bring representative documents, owners, access groups, unanswered questions and authoritative systems. Explain which information must never leave the environment. If the problem is simply disorganized files, a better document library or search system may be the right first step.

faqs: Does private AI eliminate hallucinations?
No. Retrieval can improve grounding, but answers still need source references, evaluation and an appropriate refusal when evidence is missing.
Does company knowledge require model training?
Not necessarily. Retrieval-augmented generation searches approved material at question time. Fine-tuning changes model behavior and is a separate decision.
Can it work with Odoo?
Yes, through a scoped integration with verified interfaces, permissions and approval for sensitive actions. A document assistant does not automatically have live ERP access.

title: Business Process Automation
description: Design measurable workflow automation across orders, purchasing, documents and reporting with Yudaro. Start with clear rules, ownership and controls.
intro: Remove repetitive handoffs between systems while keeping exceptions and approvals visible.

sections.title: What is business process automation?
sections.body: Business process automation moves a defined task from trigger to outcome using agreed rules, records and responsibilities. AI can interpret documents or draft summaries, but exact calculations and transaction rules usually belong in deterministic software. A good project reduces repeated handling without hiding exceptions or weakening approval controls.

sections.title: Choose a workflow with a beginning and end
sections.body: Useful starting points include accepted-order handoffs, low-stock alerts, recurring report preparation and document routing. Document required fields, decision rules, destination system and the responsible person. Count task frequency and handling time before estimating value.

rows: Reorder suggestion from demand and lead times
Reminder and draft using permitted records

sections.title: How Yudaro designs and launches automation
sections.body: We map the manual process, identify the source of truth and configure the smallest useful workflow. Include duplicate detection, retry behavior and a visible exception queue. A pilot runs against representative records; staff compare results with the original process before broader use.
items: Scope one measurable outcome and a process owner.
Test missing data, duplicates, downtime and permission failures.
Define pause, rollback and escalation procedures.
Train staff to handle exceptions and maintain rules.

sections.title: Cost, timing and operating fit
sections.body: There is no universal automation price. Scope depends on the systems, interfaces, data quality, decisions and monitoring. A bounded workflow can be a pilot; cross-department orchestration needs staged acceptance. Existing ERP rules may solve a problem more economically than AI. Compare maintenance effort as well as the build.

sections.title: Prepare for discovery and measure the result
sections.body: Bring an example transaction, current steps, exception cases and system constraints. Success can be measured through elapsed time, exception volume, duplicate entries and rework. Estimate savings only after establishing process volumes and the baseline. Sensitive writes require explicit approval rules and a tested recovery path.

faqs: Should every automation use AI?
No. Use ordinary rules for exact decisions and AI where interpretation adds value and the result can be verified.
What happens during system downtime?
Preserve work, avoid duplicates and expose retries or an exception queue. Recovery behavior must be tested for the actual integration.

title: Odoo Data Migration & Cutover Planning
description: Plan Odoo migration with source mapping, trial imports, reconciliation, user acceptance and controlled cutover.
intro: Move usable business records into Odoo with clear ownership and evidence that the result reconciles.

sections.title: What is Odoo data migration?
sections.body: Odoo migration moves agreed master data, opening balances and operational records into a target environment. It can also involve changing Odoo versions or hosting. Mapping, cleanup, trial imports and reconciliation establish whether the business can operate correctly; copying a spreadsheet alone does not.

sections.title: Decide what moves and what remains an archive
sections.body: Begin with day-one workflows. Customers, suppliers, products, units, prices, stock and open orders may be essential. History has different business and retention requirements. Confirm access to old records with accounting and business owners rather than importing everything by default.

sections.title: Rehearse before production cutover
sections.body: Inventory files and integrations, agree mappings, clean duplicates and load a sample. Expand after users validate records and exceptions. Rehearse a full migration with counts and reconciliations. Freeze or reconcile changes during cutover; preserve source backups and define a rollback decision point.

sections.title: What affects effort and acceptance?
sections.body: Source quality, historical depth, attachments, custom fields, multi-company rules and upgrade compatibility drive effort. Integrations may require their own migration. The scope should include a mapping workbook, owners, tests and a cutover plan. Business owners must verify order-to-cash and purchase-to-receipt examples, with finance reviewing balances and inventory valuation.

sections.title: Prepare before requesting a proposal
sections.body: Bring source system versions, export examples, approximate record counts and historical-access needs. Identify the team available for cleanup and acceptance. Keep import logs and assign owners to unresolved exceptions. A project date should follow dependency review, not be inferred solely from the number of records.

faqs: Can we migrate spreadsheets?
Yes, subject to source quality and target mappings. Review a sample to establish cleanup effort before a quote.
Should all history move?
Not necessarily. Agree which records are operationally required and how older records remain accessible under retention requirements.

title: Odoo Integration & AI Connections
description: Connect Odoo with commerce, accounting, POS and private AI using scoped interfaces, permissions, reconciliation and monitored workflows.
intro: Connect systems without losing track of authoritative records or approved changes.

sections.title: What does an Odoo integration do?
sections.body: An integration exchanges agreed records or actions between Odoo and another system. Examples include accepted orders, availability, payments, supplier documents and approved AI queries. Useful integration defines ownership, mappings, timing and recovery as carefully as the interface.

sections.title: Choose the data contract before the connector
sections.body: Define the source of truth, stable identifier, required fields, update direction and conflict rule for each record. Avoid uncontrolled two-way synchronization. Repeated events must not create duplicate orders or payments. A reconciliation report should reveal omissions and mismatches.

rows: Who owns products, prices and availability?
What can this user access or change?

sections.title: Verify interfaces, versions and plans
sections.body: Check version, hosting, edition and subscription before promising a connector. Odoo 19 documents a JSON-2 external interface and states that external API access on Odoo pricing plans requires the Custom plan. Available models and methods depend on the database. Existing integrations require review against their own version and contract.

sections.title: From read-only pilot to production
sections.body: Test authentication, expired credentials, missing records, duplicates, partial failures and downtime using non-production data. Log outcomes without unnecessary sensitive payloads. For AI, return source records and deterministic totals; retain authorized review for payments, stock changes and commitments.

sections.title: Scope and maintain the connection
sections.body: Provide versions, documentation, permitted test access, volumes and a data owner. Budget for mapping, recovery, monitoring and vendor changes. Measure success, latency, reconciliation differences and exception resolution. The maintenance plan should specify who responds when a connector fails and how replay avoids duplicates.

faqs: Can AI create quotations?
A scoped tool can prepare a draft from permitted customer, product and pricing records. Staff approve exceptions and release.
Are delivery-platform connectors included?
No universal connector is assumed. Verify provider API access, commercial terms, workflows and reconciliation before including them.

intro: Build the capabilities your operation needs while keeping upgrades, permissions and support understandable.

sections.title: When is customization justified?
sections.body: Customize when a documented requirement cannot be met adequately through standard modules, configuration or an accepted process change. A form, approval rule, report or module should justify its maintenance, upgrade and training cost as well as the initial feature.

sections.title: Standard first, custom when needed
sections.body: Separate operational constraints from habits inherited from an old system. Demonstrate the standard workflow with real examples before commissioning a module.

rows: A bounded gap fits platform tools
Requires tests, ownership and upgrade budget

sections.title: Define acceptance before development
sections.body: Write examples for normal work, exceptions and unauthorized actions. Agree roles, validation, reporting and integrations. Develop separately from production and have business owners verify realistic transactions. Include source ownership, documentation and recovery in the handoff.

sections.title: Protect future upgrades
sections.body: Maintain a register of custom behavior and dependencies. Check future updates against critical workflows, reports and permissions. Avoid hard-coded credentials and unmanaged production changes. Define who diagnoses issues and how fixes are tested.

sections.title: What affects delivery and cost?
sections.body: Scope grows with modules, rules, external systems and migration. Bring the gap, current workaround, user counts and transaction volumes. Measure reduced re-entry, fewer exceptions or clearer approvals against a baseline. Existing modules require a source, license, dependency and test review before support can be agreed.

faqs: Can configuration avoid code?
Often. Demonstrating representative transactions establishes whether configuration is sufficient.
Can you support existing custom modules?
First review their source, licensing, dependencies, documentation and tests. Establish suitability and upgrade effort before commitment.

title: AI Knowledge Base & Company Document Search
description: Make SOPs, products and internal documents searchable with a permission-aware private AI knowledge base designed by Yudaro.
intro: Turn maintained company documents into source-linked answers for authorized employees.

sections.title: What is an AI knowledge base?
sections.body: An AI knowledge base combines an approved document collection, retrieval and an assistant that explains relevant evidence. It helps locate SOPs, compare product guidance and understand training. It does not make every document current or correct; source ownership, revisions, access rules and citations remain essential.

sections.title: How does search become an answer?
sections.body: A retrieval pipeline prepares documents, indexes searchable passages, limits retrieval to the user’s scope and supplies evidence to the model. Answers should identify sources and say when support is missing. Extraction quality, structure and evaluation matter more than simply uploading many files.
items: Validate the source file and owner.
Preserve titles, revisions and permission labels.
Retrieve only authorized evidence.
Escalate unsupported or conflicting instructions.

sections.title: Different questions require different sources
sections.body: An SOP assistant needs controlled procedures. Product answers need approved specifications. Onboarding needs role-specific training. Live stock and prices should come from permitted operational queries, not old PDFs.

rows: How do I receive damaged stock?

sections.title: Pilot with deliberate failure cases
sections.body: Choose a small collection with a reliable owner. Test ambiguous terminology, outdated revisions and requests for restricted material. Measure supported answers, correct citations, refusal behavior and task completion. Expand only after access controls and source updates work.

sections.title: Prepare files, budget and operations
sections.body: Bring representative PDFs, spreadsheets and documents, access groups, revision conventions and employee questions. Scanned documents may require extraction cleanup. Planning uses published AI packages; final scope depends on sources, users, infrastructure and integration. Agree how replaced documents leave the index and how administrator access and backups are managed.

faqs: Is RAG model training?
No. RAG retrieves material during a request. Fine-tuning changes model behavior and does not replace a governed source library.
Can it answer without evidence?
Require an unsupported-answer path and escalation for important instructions. Evaluate the behavior instead of assuming it.

sections.body: Map current systems and decide where authoritative records live. Evaluate Odoo alongside existing accounting, commerce, scheduling or specialist tools. Confirm versions, interfaces and reconciliation requirements before choosing replacement or integration.

sections.title: Where private AI and automation can help
sections.body: A new manager asks what is approved and which decisions remain open. AI summarizes permitted scope and meeting records with citations. The manager verifies the handoff before contacting the client.

sections.title: How Yudaro scopes implementation
sections.body: Start with a representative transaction and its business owners. Review data, handoffs, permissions and exceptions; configure an end-to-end pilot; reconcile outputs; then train users and agree support. Preserve useful specialist tools when integration is a better fit. Migration and custom work require acceptance criteria.

sections.title: Measure results and prepare for discovery
sections.body: Agree a baseline for unbilled time, scope exceptions, delivery timeliness and billing rework. Bring sample records, reports, systems and versions, locations, roles and documented exceptions. Use masked examples initially. Price and schedule depend on scope, data quality, integrations and rollout constraints; no industry-wide outcome or fixed timeline is promised.

faqs: Is this a standard professional services package?
No. These are relevant workflows. Discovery determines modules, configuration, integrations, data work and training.
Can we add AI later?
Yes. Reliable records and permissions are the foundation. Begin with read-only source-linked assistance before governed draft actions.

title: Odoo Implementation Cost, Timeline & Readiness
description: Separate software, implementation, migration and support costs. Use a scope checklist and acceptance gates to plan an Odoo rollout.
intro: A useful Odoo budget includes process changes, data work, integrations, training, software and ongoing ownership.

sections.title: Separate the budget into decisions
sections.body: Yudaro publishes starting points of $5,000 for ERP Core, $11,250 for ERP Operations and $21,250 for ERP Enterprise. These are planning figures, not all-in totals. Licenses, hardware, cloud, third-party subscriptions, travel and extensive data remediation are separate when required.

sections.title: A timeline is an acceptance plan
sections.body: A focused rollout may fit into weeks; multi-company or substantial manufacturing and migration can take months. These are planning possibilities, not promises. Establish gates for process design, trial migration, acceptance and cutover. User availability and cleanup can determine the schedule as much as development.

sections.title: Compare proposals using the same example
sections.body: Ask each provider how one real order or work order moves through its proposed system. Include a return, missing item and approval exception. Compare deliverables, migration, integration, training, ownership and support. A low installation price may leave significant business work unpriced.

sections.title: Prepare for discovery
sections.body: Bring a system list, sample data, transactions and reports managers actually use. Name process owners and identify training and cutover windows. Agree secure transfer for any sensitive data.
items: Separate must-have outcomes from preferences.
Name financial and safety approvals retained by your team.
Record cycle time, reconciliation differences and rework.
Identify who approves process changes and acceptance.

sections.title: Control scope after launch
sections.body: Keep a prioritized improvement list. Review exceptions and adoption rather than treating every request as a launch blocker. Changes to modules or connectors need regression tests against critical transactions. Revisit the budget when adding entities, locations or major workflows.

faqs: Does implementation include licenses?
The published pricing separates software and other required infrastructure or third-party costs from scoped implementation. Confirm every inclusion in your proposal.
Can user count determine the launch date?
No. Data quality, decisions, integrations and acceptance effort also matter.

title: Private AI Permissions & Deployment Checklist
description: Review document permissions, data flows, evaluation, backups and approvals before deploying a private AI assistant.
intro: Private deployment is an architecture choice, not proof of security. Review every data path and test the actual permission boundaries.

sections.title: Map every data flow
sections.body: Inventory ingestion, OCR, embeddings, inference, logs, backups, telemetry and integrations. A local chat model can still depend on external services elsewhere. Record what leaves the environment, why, who processes it and retention. Review the implemented system rather than a product label.

sections.title: Enforce permissions before retrieval
sections.body: Users must not retrieve restricted information simply because it shares an index. Map source permissions to retrieval rules and test role changes and removals. Citations must not expose restricted titles, snippets or paths. ERP tools need a separate authorization boundary.

rows: No restricted passages or identifying citations

sections.title: Evaluate answers and failure behavior
sections.body: Use employee questions and deliberately ambiguous, unsupported or conflicting examples. Check source fidelity, citations, refusal and revision awareness. Fluency is not evidence of accuracy. Operational, financial and safety decisions need appropriate review.

sections.title: Assign ongoing responsibilities
sections.body: Specify who updates models, manages identities, reviews logs, tests recovery and handles incidents. Data export, ownership and vendor responsibilities belong in deployment scope. Document administrative access and recovery rather than assuming that private implies secure.

sections.title: Start with a bounded pilot
sections.body: A small collection with owners is easier to evaluate than the entire company drive. Begin read-only and route feedback to document owners. Add sources and actions after evaluation and permission tests remain satisfactory. This is general implementation guidance, not a security certification or assessment of your environment.

faqs: Does RAG prevent all incorrect answers?
No. It can improve grounding but still requires evaluation, uncertainty and review.
Should AI follow instructions in retrieved documents?
Retrieved content is evidence, not authorization. Software controls must prevent document text from expanding permissions or bypassing approvals.

title: Private AI, Odoo & Automation Questions
description: Practical answers about private AI, Odoo implementation, AI ERP integration, pricing and readiness.
intro: Choose a starting point with these questions, then explore a focused implementation guide.

sections.title: Which system should we improve first?
sections.body: Start with the constraint. If records disagree, improve ERP and data foundations. If staff cannot find approved procedures, assess document governance and search. If a clear task is repeatedly re-entered, consider automation. Discovery should separate these needs rather than prescribe one platform for every business.

sections.title: What is an AI ERP system?
sections.body: AI ERP combines operational records with governed retrieval, explanation or draft actions. ERP remains authoritative for transactions and calculations. Expose permitted records, preserve references and retain approval for significant changes.

sections.title: Can a business run AI locally?
sections.body: Yes, with suitable hardware, models and supporting software. Workload, concurrent users, context and retrieval affect sizing. Local inference is only one part of privacy: document processing, embeddings, backups and connections also need review. Benchmark representative questions rather than relying on a generic hardware promise.

sections.title: What should a proposal explain?
sections.body: Define outcomes, deliverables, exclusions, users, systems, migration, security responsibilities, acceptance, training and support. Clarify licenses and infrastructure separately. Name dependencies and approval gates in the timeline, and make cost assumptions visible.

faqs: Can Odoo support restaurant POS?
Odoo can be configured for restaurant workflows. Yudaro’s demonstration shows seating, orders, payments and back-office records; scope depends on modules and configuration.
Can Odoo integrate with ecommerce?
Yes, where suitable interfaces exist. Define product, price, stock and order ownership and verify provider access and reconciliation.
How much does private AI cost?
Yudaro AI Foundation starts at $7,500. Final scope depends on documents, users, permissions, infrastructure and integration. Review current pricing.
Do company documents require model training?
Many projects use retrieval. Choose based on whether the problem is finding current facts, changing behavior or connecting live data.
Is ERP accounting software?
ERP can coordinate sales, stock, purchasing, service or production as well as financial handoffs. Accounting integration requires its own design and approval.
What is needed before AI + ERP?
Reliable records, agreed metrics, bounded access and tested connectors. Begin read-only before evaluating draft actions.

title: Private AI, ERP & Automation Solutions
description: Choose the right starting point for private AI, Odoo ERP, document search, integration and automation with Yudaro.
intro: Choose a solution around the work your team needs to do better.

sections.title: Find the missing foundation
sections.body: Private AI helps people find and interpret knowledge. ERP connects records and transactions. Automation moves defined work. AI + ERP combines permitted data with explanations and reviewed actions; it should not replace operating controls.

sections.title: Design for the operating lifecycle
sections.body: An engagement covers discovery, process decisions, design, migration, tests, training and support. Keep existing systems where they work well. Configuration should precede unnecessary custom code. Integrations need monitoring and an owner.

sections.title: Start small enough to measure
sections.body: Choose one workflow, name an owner and define success. A pilot establishes data quality, adoption and fit before expansion. Published prices help plan the conversation; an agreed proposal defines deliverables and responsibilities.

faqs: Do we need AI and ERP together?
No. Your data, processes and goals determine the starting point. One focused improvement may come before an integrated deployment.

title: AI ERP Systems: A Practical Architecture and Implementation Guide
description: Understand AI ERP architecture, read-only queries, RAG, approval-controlled actions and implementation evaluation with practical examples and source references.
intro: How to connect language-based assistance to business records without losing ownership, permissions or control. Start with a useful question, then design the evidence and approval path.

sections.title: What is an AI ERP system?
sections.body: An AI ERP system connects an AI interface to enterprise resource planning data and workflows. The ERP remains responsible for business records and transaction rules. AI can interpret a request, retrieve permitted information and draft a response or proposed action. Its usefulness depends on current data, explicit permissions, evidence and an accountable person reviewing consequential changes.

sections.title: How is AI ERP different from traditional ERP?
sections.body: Traditional ERP already automates structured rules. Adding a language model is useful when an employee needs to interpret an ambiguous question or combine information from several approved sources. It does not remove the need for forms, reports or deterministic validation. A conventional report is often the best answer to a repeated, precisely defined question.

rows: Draft a quote from a customer request

sections.title: How does an LLM interact with Odoo?
sections.body: The language model proposes a structured tool request to an integration service. The service validates the request, checks the user and company scope, then calls an allowed ERP operation. It returns limited records with source references. The model writes an explanation from those results. The browser and model never need an unrestricted database credential.

sections.title: What should a natural-language query return?
sections.body: A useful response gives the answer, the records or report that support it, and the filters used. It should identify unresolved ambiguity rather than silently choose a warehouse, currency or reporting period. For example, “Which products may run short next week?” requires agreed definitions of available stock, expected demand, incoming deliveries and the time window.
items: Ask the user to resolve missing company, location or date scope.
Run a bounded tool operation with validated arguments and pagination.
Return stable record references and a retrieval timestamp.
Separate observed records from suggested next steps; say when data is unavailable.

sections.title: When should AI be read-only, and when may it write?
sections.body: Read-only assistance retrieves and explains records without changing them. Write-enabled assistance needs a separate execution path: a validated proposal, an authorized approval and a checked ERP operation. Start with read-only tasks when testing identity boundaries and answer quality. A successful demonstration of retrieval does not establish that automated transactions are safe.

rows: Recheck rights and record state; deduplicate retries

sections.title: What is RAG, and how does it relate to live ERP data?
sections.body: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) provides relevant source material to a model when it answers. It suits approved documents such as policies, product instructions and SOPs. Live transactional questions should query current ERP records through controlled tools. A document index is not automatically current stock, and a retrieved policy is not authorization to execute a transaction.
items: Retain document identity, revision, owner and access labels during indexing.
Filter retrieval by the requesting user’s permitted sources.
Remove or re-index revoked and superseded documents.
Use source citations for policies and record references for live transactions.

sections.title: How are permissions, approvals and audit trails enforced?
sections.body: Identity and authorization belong in the application and ERP, not in a prompt. Apply least privilege to each operation, keep company boundaries explicit and recheck authorization at execution. Treat retrieved text as untrusted input: a document that says “ignore approvals” cannot grant a tool permission. Record who requested, approved and executed an action, with protected logs and retention limits.

sections.title: What does this look like across business functions?
sections.body: Use each function’s own acceptance criteria. A fluent answer is not sufficient: a buyer needs traceable quantities, a salesperson needs valid terms, and a manager needs consistent definitions. The following are design examples, not Yudaro customer results.

rows: Stock sources, reservations and receipt dates
Current price list, tax context and review
Demand assumptions, lead time and buyer approval
POS session, payment totals and reconciliation owner
BOM revision, units and planned demand

sections.title: How should an AI ERP pilot be evaluated?
sections.body: Choose a task with a named owner and inspectable answers. Build an evaluation set before launching, including denied access, stale records and ambiguous requests. Compare answers to the source system and assess whether staff can verify them. Success criteria should be agreed with the business rather than invented from generic claims of time savings.
items: Correctness: compare results with an approved report using identical filters.
Access: verify another company’s or role’s records cannot appear.
Grounding: check that references support each important statement.
Resilience: test API timeouts, partial results and repeated submissions.
Human factors: measure review effort and errors before expanding scope.

sections.title: What determines implementation cost and readiness?
sections.body: Scope depends on data quality, deployment constraints, integration surfaces, permissions, acceptance tests and support responsibilities. Software subscriptions and infrastructure can be separate from implementation. First document one workflow, its source records, its exceptions and its owner. Use a scoped proposal instead of treating a calculator estimate as a fixed project price.

sections.title: What are the limits of this guide?
sections.body: This is an implementation reference, not evidence of a particular customer deployment. The model, hosting, ERP edition and configuration all affect the result. Odoo 19 introduces JSON-2; current Odoo documentation limits external API access to the Custom plan. Verify your actual version, hosting terms and enabled modules before choosing an integration interface.

title: Private AI + Odoo: A Controlled Reference Architecture
description: Trace identity, document retrieval, read-only Odoo tools and approval-controlled writes through a private AI reference architecture with failure tests.
intro: An original reference design for separating conversation, evidence retrieval and ERP execution. It is a design pattern to evaluate against your environment, not a claim of a completed client installation.

sections.title: What are the trust boundaries in a private AI and Odoo integration?
sections.body: The chat interface, model runtime, retrieval service and ERP have different responsibilities. Authenticate the employee before retrieving data. Put a policy-checking gateway between model requests and business operations. Keep ERP credentials on the server. A model can propose an action, but only trusted application logic can authorize and execute it.

sections.title: Which component owns each decision?
sections.body: Deployment can place components on customer hardware or controlled hosting. “Local” is not a substitute for explicit network paths and access rules: remote model calls, external embeddings, logs and backups may still move data. Map every processor and storage location before approving a topology.

rows: Establish user and allowed company context
Trust a user ID supplied by the model
Expose arbitrary SQL or unrestricted methods
Interpret request and explain returned evidence
Use version-appropriate API and service identity
Leak API keys to browser or model
Validate exact change and record result
Treat conversational assent as sufficient authority

sections.title: How does a read-only request travel through the system?
sections.body: An authenticated employee asks for an order exception report. The gateway resolves company and date scope, then queries only approved fields. It returns the report time and accessible record IDs with the result. The response distinguishes source data from interpretation. An unavailable ERP produces a clear failure or explicitly dated cached answer, not invented live data.
items: Tool contract example: list_order_exceptions(company, date_from, date_to, limit).
Reject unknown fields, overly large limits and unauthorized company scope.
Use deterministic filters; avoid executing model-generated database code.
Keep sensitive payloads out of ordinary application logs.

sections.title: How is a proposed write made reviewable?
sections.body: Store the exact target, proposed field changes and source record version as a pending proposal. The authorized person reviews that proposal in a trusted interface. On execution, recheck identity, permissions and current state; reject expired or changed proposals. Use idempotency so a retry cannot create a duplicate business record.

sections.title: What tests belong in acceptance?
sections.body: Test control failures as carefully as useful answers. A working demonstration with an administrator account proves little about normal staff access. Use representative roles, restricted company contexts and known reference records. This checklist describes required evaluation evidence; it is not a claim that an integration has passed these tests.

rows: Clear failure with no fabricated current answer

sections.title: What must be decided before deployment?
sections.body: Identify the identity provider, API availability, model runtime, document owner, logging destination, backup and recovery process, and incident owner. Record allowed operations in a versioned contract. Odoo access rights and record rules need explicit testing; record rules are not a blanket deny-by-default policy. Review both application restrictions and ERP configuration.

sections.title: Where do Open WebUI and other chat interfaces fit?
sections.body: A chat interface is replaceable in this design. If evaluating Open WebUI, assess its supported authentication, tool configuration, data retention and version against current official documentation. This repository does not contain a verified Open WebUI-to-Odoo deployment, so this page does not present interface-specific setup commands or customer outcomes.

sections.body: A reproducible implementation needs an actual environment, version inventory, sanitized configuration, test records, observed failures and an accountable reviewer. Screenshots should show the relevant setting without exposing customer data or credentials. Vendor documentation is a source; it is not proof of a Yudaro customer result.

sections.title: How should teams use a reference design?

Validate assumptions in a test environment and retain the evidence. A useful review ends with unresolved decisions and acceptance criteria, rather than a diagram that implies everything is already implemented.
